newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swiss cantons back humanitarian fund plans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swiss cantons back humanitarian fund plans.

text.p: Finance directors from Switzerland's cantons backed the federal government's plan to create a seven billion Swiss franc ($4.9 billion) humanitarian fund to be financed with official gold reserves, but attached some strings.

The plan, which must still be approved by parliament and Swiss voters in a referendum next year, calls for distributing around 350 million Swiss francs a year in Switzerland and abroad to victims of human rights abuses and disasters.

It is separate from a 265 million Swiss franc Holocaust memorial fund that Swiss banks, other private businesses and the SNB are financing to alleviate the suffering of needy Holocaust survivors and their families.
Directors adopted a resolution supporting the foundation in principle, but said its goals had to be clarified, the Swiss SDA news agency reported from the officials' annual meeting.

The cantons also want to protect their claims to Swiss National Bank (SNB) assets by insisting that the central bank manage all gold revaluation profits and that revaluation profits not used for the foundation had to remain with the SNB, it said.

"The Conference of Cantonal Finance Directors (FDK) supports the government's intention to create the Solidarity Foundation in 1998 as testimony to Switzerland's humanitarian tradition," the politically influential group said in a statement.

At the end of last year, cantons, cantonal banks and other public authorities and institutions held 63 percent of the SNB's shares. Private shareholders had 37 percent, of which 70 percent were individials and 30 percent legal entities.

Some cantonal officials have grumbled that they should have been consulted before Swiss President Arnold Koller announced plans in March to revalue and sell some of Switzerland's gold reserves to finance the foundation.

Opinion polls taken immediately after the announcement in March showed most Swiss backed the idea of creating the humanitarian fund, which Berne hopes will clear the air of allegations Switzerland cooly profited from World War Two.
But resistance to the idea has been growing, fuelled by charges from right-wing politicians that Switzerland is being unjustly blackmailed from abroad. ($ = 1.432 Swiss Francs)
